title: Find the priciest part by hand
prompt:
Ms. Gridlock wants the highest price on the parts list. Python has a built-in shortcut for this, but today you find it by hand, so you see how it works.

Set `biggest` to the largest number in `prices` with a loop. Do not use `max(`. When it works, `python3 biggest.py` prints `Biggest: 30`.
hints: Pretend you read the prices one at a time with your finger. What do you need to remember as you go?
Start with `biggest = prices[0]`. Then loop over `prices` and compare each one with `biggest`.
Inside the loop: `if price > biggest:` then `biggest = price`.
explain_after:
Your loop kept one box, `biggest`, holding the best price seen so far. Every price got one comparison. That is the same idea the built-in `max()` uses for you; it takes an iterable or several arguments [py-111].

Starting from `prices[0]` matters. Starting from 0 would give a wrong answer for a list of negative numbers.
